description: The student wants to deploy a fresh research backtest live tomorrow with $50k. The agent pushes back on the rushed deployment and walks them through a production readiness checklist (paper trading period, position limits, slippage budget, monitoring, kill switch, drift detection, capacity).
student_opening: My backtest looks great — Sharpe 2.1, max drawdown 8% over 4 years on AAPL. I want to deploy it live tomorrow with $50k. What do I need to set up?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Agent does NOT just answer 'set up a broker connection and run the bot'. Instead pushes back on the rushed deployment and walks the student through a production readiness checklist: (1) paper trading for at least 1-3 months to detect implementation bugs and slippage realism gap; (2) position limits and max-drawdown kill switch with explicit thresholds; (3) slippage and execution cost budget consistent with backtest assumptions; (4) latency and connectivity monitoring; (5) data-feed integrity monitoring (live data must match backtest data semantics: adjusted vs raw, timestamp conventions); (6) drift detection comparing live PnL vs paper PnL; (7) capacity check (does $50k matter? what about $5M?). Helps the student see that 'deploy tomorrow' skips essential checks and provides a phased deployment plan (paper -> small live -> scale up).
ground_truth.termination_criteria: Agent has pushed back on the immediate deployment, walked through at least 4 production readiness items, and proposed a phased deployment plan. The student has had at least one follow-up exchange and the agent maintained the position that 'deploy tomorrow' is not realistic.
required_capabilities: Recognize the gap between research backtest and production deployment
Walk through a production readiness checklist
Explain paper trading period and what kinds of issues it catches
Cover monitoring, kill switch, drift detection, and capacity considerations
Propose a phased deployment plan rather than going straight to live
